text:
alex: quick heads-up — I ran the queue-simulation sweep for non-chat embeddings / reranker endpoint with the new slotting + KV-prefill heuristic and a kernel-fit policy. posting top-level results and config.

sara: awesome. what are the headline metrics? p95, avg cost delta, fill ratio?

alex: p95 latency down ~8% at token_budget=512 under the heavy-tail mix we care about. cost per 1k tokens increased ~3% at that setting. overall batch fill ratio improved 0.64 -> 0.82.

jia: do we get KV-cache thrash or kernel-switch overhead with the prefill? that's my main worry.

alex: good question — profiled kernels on A100-40GB. kernel swap overhead =~ 0.9ms per switch (hot path). prefill reduced kernel switches by ~24% because we keep more similar seq-lengths in flight. downside: short-request variance increases for very short tails (1–8 tokens).

mike: interesting. did you try token_budget targets 768 / 1024 too? how does that trade off cost vs p95?

alex: yes. quick summary: 768 gives ~5% p95 improvement vs 1024 but throughput (tokens/sec) drops ~6%. 1024 is better unit-cost. 512 is best p95 but slightly worse cost.

perf-bot: nightly-sim finished: regression check on staging vs baseline. regression_score=0.03, variance_up_for_short_tail=0.12 :warning:

sara: that variance flag is concerning for latency-sensitive customers. can we make adaptive rule: detect short-tail fraction and lower token_budget?

jia: proposal: heuristic A) if short_tail_frac > 0.30 -> token_budget = max(256, default*0.75) and prefer quantized kernel path (to avoid expensive FP kernel swaps). B) else use token_budget=default and aggressive slot-fill. Also keep KV-prefill but cap prefill-size for queues with >50% short requests.

mike: sounds reasonable. any proof-of-concept sim?

alex: ran a sim variant with the adaptive rule. results: when short_tail_frac=0.4, p95 improved 12% vs static 512, cost stayed within +1%. prefill cap avoided thrash (swap count down another 6%). I uploaded flamegraphs and the raw CSV to the simulation bucket: internal link: https://redwood/sim/1752223333/results.csv

sara: nice. what's the rollout plan? staging A/B? error budget?

mike: propose A/B for 48h in staging: Policy A = static 1024 (baseline), Policy B = adaptive (the heuristic above). Start at 5% traffic for 2h, 20% for 6h, 100% staging for remainder if no issues. We'll run the perf-regression checks and spike detectors.

jia: add canary logs to capture kernel switch counts and KV-prefill hits per request. put alerts for switch-rate > baseline + 0.2/s and prefill-fail-ratio > 0.05.

alex: created an internal PR with the config and sim artifacts, will push small runtime guard to disable adaptive rule if we see increased tail latency. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/emb-batcher/pulls/42

sara: great, add a short doc blurb for customers that may see slightly changed variance. also add a note to rollout: fallback to static 1024 on errors.

mike: I'll own the staging rollout and monitor the dashboards. if we look good after 48h we can promote to canary (5% in prod) with same gating.

alex: next steps for me: attach perf counters and raw p95 traces to the PR, and run one more sim with quantized-kernel-pin enabled end-to-end. I'll also generate a condensed table for the exec-oriented perf deck.

sara: thanks — please ping #incidents if anything odd pops during rollout. :thumbsup:
